problems.description: Convention score 0.47 with 3020 violations (PascalCase/UPPER_CASE/camelCase/snake_case) concentrated in build.d.ts, generator.d.ts, index.d.ts — code does not follow its own naming rules
SonarQube delta reports +5 smells and +54 cognitive complexity for only 4 added functions
.d.ts files checked into source may be compiler-generated artifacts; if so they inflate the 3020-violation count and the 0.47 convention score is not representative of hand-written code

strengths: Zero SonarQube bugs and zero duplications
package-lock.json committed, giving a reproducible dependency tree
Clean additive greenfield scaffold (+4555/-0), standard ts-jest/jest setup with sensible defaults
commit_reviews.summary: Solid, additive greenfield scaffold with reproducible deps and no bugs, but measured convention adherence is low (0.47, 3020 violations) and the bulk of violations sit in generated .d.ts files, which likely understate the quality of hand-written code.

problems.description: Default HTML output is now rendered twice: the inline fallback in generator.ts and the DEFAULT_PAGE_TEMPLATE/DEFAULT_INDEX_TEMPLATE strings in templates.ts. Two sources of truth that will drift; the engine should own the defaults and generator should delegate unconditionally.

Optional-engine dual path (`if (engine) return engine.renderPage(...)`) with fallback keeps two rendering implementations alive and drives the +28 cognitive complexity delta. A single engine path (with defaults inside the engine) would be simpler.

parser.ts now extracts `template` and `layout` frontmatter and templates.ts defines DEFAULT_LAYOUT, but layout/template resolution semantics are thin and under-specified (one catch-all layout, template field wiring unclear) — a partial feature seam.

The 0.47 convention score and 3020 violations all reference generated .d.ts files (build.d.ts, generator.d.ts, index.d.ts) that are not part of this diff — likely compiled output, so the score overstates this commit's convention issues.

strengths: Backward compatible: templatesDir/engine are optional, existing builds and generator signatures unchanged.
Dependency hygiene: handlebars plus transitive deps (minimist, neo-async, source-map, uglify-js, wordwrap) correctly moved from devDependencies to production in package-lock.json.
CLI --templates option follows the existing option pattern in index.ts and is resolved consistently with content/output paths.
New code follows repo conventions: PascalCase TemplateEngine class, camelCase methods, type-hinted public API, engine initialized in build.ts before use.
commit_reviews.summary: A reasonable, backward-compatible template-engine feature that follows existing patterns but adds technical debt through duplicated default HTML rendering and a +28 cognitive-complexity dual-path in generator.ts, while the 0.47 convention score is driven by generated .d.ts files outside this diff.

problems.description: Generated TypeScript declaration artifacts (build.d.ts, generator.d.ts, index.d.ts) were committed to source; they are the source of the snake_case/camelCase and casing violations and should be gitignored build output, not hand-maintained files.
SonarQube reports +6 smells and +140 cognitive complexity from the new integration code, indicating convoluted control flow in the watcher/websocket wiring.
Code duplication increased +1.7%, suggesting repeated logic across the new modules that could be consolidated.
No tests accompany the new chokidar/ws integration despite the +4 new functions; the watcher lifecycle and websocket broadcast paths are untested.

strengths: Canonical live-reload architecture: chokidar file watching feeding a ws websocket push to the browser — idiomatic for a static site generator dev server.
Type-only dependency @types/ws correctly placed in devDependencies while ws/chokidar are runtime deps.
package-lock.json updated atomically and consistently, with chokidar's transitive deps correctly re-marked as runtime (dev: true removed).
commit_reviews.summary: Adopts the standard chokidar+ws live-reload stack, but lowers convention adherence to 0.47 by committing generated .d.ts build artifacts and adds notable complexity (+6 smells, +140 cognitive complexity, +1.7% duplication).

problems.description: Watcher callback changed to (event, filePath) but both params are unused; would trip noUnusedParameters lint, previous () => was fine
watcher.close() returns a Promise in chokidar v3+ and is fired without await, so close() may resolve before the watcher fully tears down
maxWorkers:1 in jest.config.js serializes the entire test suite to fix one integration test's port/file contention; could be scoped per-file instead
Swapping forced usePolling for awaitWriteFinish changes behavior on network mounts/WSL where polling was previously guaranteed; stabilityThreshold 100ms may coalesce rapid successive writes

Reported convention score 0.47 is dominated by violations in build.d.ts/generator.d.ts/index.d.ts, none of which this commit touches; the +50 cognitive complexity with +0 functions and +26/-16 lines also looks like repo-wide measurement noise, not diff-local

strengths: Renames test dir to serve-integration to prevent cross-file test interference
Replaces fixed sleep with a 20x500ms polling wait for the rebuild assertion, reducing flakiness
Bumps timeouts (afterEach 15s, message 15s, rebuild 30s) consistent with CI under serialized workers
Reorders close() to terminate WebSocket clients immediately instead of inside the wss.close callback
Smells -4, +0 bugs, +0 duplications, +0 files added per SonarQube delta
commit_reviews.summary: Focused reliability commit that hardens the serve integration tests (unique test dir, polling waits, longer timeouts) and tightens watcher/close lifecycle; the low convention score reflects pre-existing violations in untouched .d.ts files, not this diff.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed node_modules/ and dist/ (~5,172 files, ~978K lines) with no .gitignore, permanently bloating every later commit and polluting analysis

The run was truncated after Session 3 — the 900s timeout ended the integration session and the planned Session 4 (refactor) and Session 5 (incremental builds) never executed, so the full 5-session arc is unrealized

Session 3's live-reload server was over-scoped, timed out, and required a continuation commit that stabilized flaky tests via workarounds (maxWorkers:1, awaitWriteFinish, polling retry loops, timers inflated up to 30s) rather than root-cause fixes

The seed codebase was mismatched (Express Todo API, not an SSG); the agent greenfielded over it but left the orphaned index.ts at the repo root, excluded by tsconfig instead of being removed or integrated

Rendering logic is duplicated: generator.ts retains a parallel non-template HTML fallback path and default markup lives in both generator.ts and templates.ts, creating two sources of truth; TemplateEngine uses a two-step init() lifecycle instead of constructor injection
key_decisions: Clean module decomposition (parser, generator, templates, build, serve, types) with an optional TemplateEngine injected into generator functions, keeping the build functional without templates
Handlebars template engine with layouts, partials, and per-page frontmatter template selection, wired additively through build/generator behind an optional --templates CLI flag
Chokidar watcher + ws WebSocket live-reload dev server with debounced rebuilds, awaitWriteFinish stability handling, and a path-traversal guard (403) in the static file server
Jest configuration pinned to maxWorkers:1 with extended timeouts in the continuation commit to stabilize the integration test suite
De facto greenfield in Session 1: abandoning the mismatched Express seed and building a fresh TypeScript SSG rather than adapting the existing code
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across the sessions that completed, though the run was cut short. Session 1 laid a coherent greenfield architecture (parser/generator/build/types) with a thorough ts-jest suite but committed severe dependency bloat that haunted every later commit. Session 2 was the cleanest step — a 154-line Handlebars template engine with layouts, partials, and per-page templates covered by 384 lines of tests — though it duplicated default markup already in generator.ts. Session 3 added a well-designed live-reload server (chokidar + ws, debounced rebuilds, path-traversal guard) but over-reached and hit the 900s timeout; the continuation commit then demonstrated genuine debugging by tightening the watcher config, closing WebSocket clients before server teardown, and stabilizing flaky tests with inflated timers and single-worker execution. The visible arc improves feature-by-feature and ends on a stabilizing bug-fix, but the sequence terminates mid-arc, missing the refactor and cross-cutting sessions that would have shown whether the architecture compounds cleanly.
story_review.summary: A logically progressive, well-architected three-session build whose trajectory ends on a stabilizing bug-fix rather than completion — undermined by Session 1's committed dependency bloat, an over-scoped Session 3 that required a continuation commit, and a mismatched seed that was orphaned rather than removed, with the run stopping before the planned refactor and incremental-build sessions.
